messages:
Sara Chen: Quick sync — API team flagged a couple edge cases for audit event names when requests come from external connectors. Need alignment on namespace + visibility.
Miguel Alvarez: Can you paste an example? are these connector-originated events marked differently today?
Sara Chen: Example they saw: `connector.request.create` and `connector.apikey.rotate` coming through as the same top-level service. Confusing for downstream SIEM.
Priya Kapoor: Two quick concerns: (1) customer-visible event names vs internal-only, (2) embedding raw KMS key IDs in events. Both are current pain points.
Alex B: For namespacing, we recommend `<actor>.<resource>.<action>` e.g. `external_connector.integration.create` to separate external actors from internal services.
Jenna Ops: +1 but we need a clear rule for multi-actor events: e.g., when an org admin triggers a connector on behalf of a user. How do we surface initiator vs subject?
Sara Chen: Proposal: include `actor.type` and `actor.id` in payload, and keep event name focused on the resource/action. Event name should not try to encode actor role.
Miguel Alvarez: Agreed. Also we should standardize suffixes for lifecycle events: `.create`, `.update`, `.delete`, `.rotate`, `.accessed`.
Priya Kapoor: About KMS: we must never emit full key material or  UUIDs that map to customer keys. Instead emit `kms.key_ref` with hashed token or opaque identifier and a `kms.key_scope` like `customer|platform`.
Alex B: Example snippet we can validate against:
```
{
  "event": "external_connector.integration.create",
  "actor": {"type": "user", "id": "U123"},
  "subject": {"type": "integration", "id": "INT-9876"},
  "kms": {"key_ref": "kp_****", "key_scope": "customer"},
  "schema_version": "audit.v2.1"
}
```
Jenna Ops: For RBAC changes: when permissions change we should emit both `rbac.binding.update` and a more granular `rbac.role.assignment.add` or `.remove` depending on the operation.
Sara Chen: Also we need to mark events that are customer-visible vs internal-only. Suggest `visibility` field with values `customer`, `platform`, `both`.
Miguel Alvarez: For backwards compatibility, new `schema_version` should be required. Consumers will reject unknown versions by default but we should publish a migration guide.
Priya Kapoor: One edge: bulk operations (e.g., `integration.bulk_import`) — should produce one summary event + per-item detail events? security team prefers per-item for auditability but that may flood logs.
Alex B: Compromise: emit `bulk.summary` + link to a `bulk.item_sample` list with sampling, plus an option to enable `full_detail` for Dedicated/Private customers.
Jenna Ops: Validation checklist before rollout: schema linting (jsonschema), sample events from API staging, SIEM mapping tests, and verify no PII/KMS leakage.
Sara Chen: Action items:
- Miguel: draft jsonschema updates for `audit.v2.1` covering `visibility` and `kms.key_ref` format (due EOD Thu).
- Priya: write KMS redaction rules & sample mappings (due Mon).
- Alex: update API docs with recommended naming patterns and multi-actor guidance (due Fri).
- Jenna: coordinate SIEM mapping test with infra (due next week).
Miguel Alvarez: I'll open a PR with schema and add a few example messages from the staging logs.
audit-bot: New schema `audit.v2.1` draft created by Miguel (link: https://git.redwood/schemas/audit/v2.1) :package:
Priya Kapoor: One more thing — customer-facing docs should have a clear migration note and examples of how to interpret namespaced events in SIEMs.
Sara Chen: Great. If no objections I'll turn this into a spec doc and we can run a cross-team review during next Thurs sync. :thumbsup:
Miguel Alvarez: No objections from me.
Alex B: LGTM.
Jenna Ops: Sounds good.
Priya Kapoor: fine by me.
Sara Chen: Thanks all — closing thread, will post the spec link when ready. :rocket:
